- [Further usage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_status_and_usage_of_the_euro) | The **euro area** ( **EA**),[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurozone#cite_note-8) commonly called the **eurozone** ( **EZ**), is a [currency union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monetary_union) of 21 [member states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_state_of_the_European_Union) of the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union) (EU) that have adopted the [euro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro) ( [€](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro_sign)) as their primary [currency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Currency) and sole [legal tender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_tender), and have thus fully implemented [Economic and Monetary Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_and_Monetary_Union_of_the_European_Union) policies. [[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurozone#cite_note-15) Within the European Union (EU), six member states have not yet adopted the euro and continue to use their own national currencies: the [Czech Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech_Republic), [Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark), [Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary), [Poland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poland), [Romania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romania), and [Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden). ## Territory ### Eurozone | [State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_state_of_the_European_Union) | [ISO code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1) | [Adopted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enlargement_of_the_eurozone)
